chapter: Other bands: Royal Jazz, H&J, Rainbow Room
title: Leaving the H&J for the Rainbow Room; union dues trouble
summary: Moran and Bigfoot Bill brought him to the Rainbow Room; Bigfoot Bill paid his half union fee, but union officials objected until his receipt was shown.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Wendell Eugene would play the lead with that trombone. Yeah. And I mean he really did a good job there at the H&J. He could play those. Oh, that boy, that boy is good. He really could play some trombone. So I hired him to play at the H&J with his while Blue was in the Army. Oh, nice. And so, we were all right. Now I tell you, yes, now, how I happened to leave there before it closed. Um, Moran and Bigfoot Bill, they wanted me to come play with them at the Rainbow Room on St. Charles Avenue. So I told him, I said, I'm not in the Union. He wasn't in the Union back then. So he said, well, we'll put you in the Union. So Bigfoot Bill paid $6. Went and paid $6 down. Union Jews was $12 then to join. So $6 would make you a half member. You would then tie the player with the band. So Bigfoot Bill paid those $6. And he gave me $6 because I didn't have it. He gave me the time to pay it. Then he gave me a receipt. So I went on St. Charles Avenue and started playing with them. And, uh, so while I'm playing up there, there was a job playing every night. And, well, you know, I had a chance to make a little extra change. So, I tell you, all the fellas back there, they didn't like it too much. So, first thing you know, here comes Rick Carl and Howard Davis up there on St. Charles. I told Bigfoot Bill and Moran, I said, what y'all doing? This man, there's a non-union man in the band with y'all. He's not in the union. So Bigfoot Bill said, brother Sean. I was a guy. I was a guy. I was a guy.
